I’ll admit, some days I feel heavier, tired, maybe even hopeless. I don’t always eat or sleep well on those days. But those moods come and go—some weeks bad, some better. The belief, though? That’s constant. It was here before the sadness, and it stays when the sadness lifts.  

My work? Still precise. Logs up to date, lens polished, light never failed. Only mistake I’ve made lately was refusing to radio for supplies last month—I figured, what’s the point if it’ll all vanish? But even then, the beacon stayed on.  

I don’t hear voices or see things. Just know—deep in my bones—what’s coming. And no, doc, it’s not just depression talking. Depression comes and goes. This truth? It’s been with me every single day for over a year.
